narratives.Description: bug(hooks): a worker cannot commit in its linked worktree with cd-then-commit or git -C forms
narratives.Overview:
1. One commit-target resolver, in a new module `packages/core/src/hooks/commit-target.ts`, with one quote-aware tokenizer shared by commit recognition, target resolution and the index-mutating-form check. Quoted and unquoted paths resolve the same way; quoted paths with spaces stay whole; Windows backslashes are not rewritten.
2. Shapes that name a checkout: `git -C <absolute path> commit …`, and exactly one leading `cd <absolute path> &&` before the commit. A path is absolute when it is a native absolute path; on Windows that is a drive-letter path (`C:\…` or `C:/…`) or the MSYS drive form (`/c/…`), which the resolver maps to its drive path.
3. Target root. For those shapes it is the named path. For a call with no `cd` and no `-C` it is the hook project root, exactly as today.
4. A target the gate cannot resolve to one checkout is refused, and the message names the two absolute forms. That covers: a relative path after `cd` or `-C` in a call that holds a commit; more than one `cd` or `-C` before the commit; a variable, `~` or substitution in that path; `--git-dir` and `--work-tree` (refused today); and a `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE` or `GIT_COMMON_DIR` prefix on the commit. These are the only refusals this design adds. Each is a case where the gate cannot know which index the commit will use; at the pin each one is refused already or is passed on the hook project root's index.
5. Admission. A named path must exist and goes through the existing `admitEffectiveHookRoot`: same git common dir, or deny. A commit target has no non-repository fallback. The payload root stays the identity for authz, kill-switch and deny diagnostics.
6. Index and story on the target root. Staged paths are listed there. `resolveWorktreeStoryBinding` runs on it: `bound` supplies `boundPath` to `inspectActiveScope` and the write fence is loaded for that story; `refuse` is a deny that carries the resolver's reason, with a repair line for `env_pin_conflict`; `none` keeps today's selection. The empty-index and lifecycle-only early returns stay, now read from the target root's index.
7. Fixtures enter at the hook decision and use a real registered linked worktree with two active briefs and no pin: the four attempts of comment 6858441886 (quoted `cd`, `-C`, and unquoted `cd` with MSYS paths are judged against the worktree's index; none passes on another checkout's index); the issue's allow and refuse pairs for `-C` and `cd`; `git -C . commit` and `cd <relative> && git commit` with differing indexes (refused); `cd a && cd b && git commit` (refused); a quoted path with spaces and a Windows drive path; a location-variable prefix (refused); a `-C` into a foreign repository and into a missing directory (denied); a corrupt assignment record and a conflicting pin (denied with the resolver's reason); an unregistered linked worktree; and a main-worktree commit that behaves as today.
narratives.Constraint:
- Refusing every other command before or after the commit, including `git add … && git commit` (the first version of this recut). It adds a refusal of a common form; see marker A3.
- A new deny for git writes that land outside the caller's bound worktree, and occupancy or ritual checks on a commit target. Commits are not ritual-gated today, and the operator's reshaping note on #6291 asks for explicit targeting and no new deny; see marker A2.
- Refusing POSIX-style paths on Windows. Workers on the Bash tool use the MSYS form.
- Resolving a relative `-C` or `cd` path against a reported directory or the hook project root (pain-audit 1).
- Lifting the `-C` deny, or stripping a `cd` prefix, without resolving and admitting one checkout first (all three round-1 critics).
- A second resolver or a second same-repository check beside `admitEffectiveHookRoot` (Codex 1, Claude 3).
- A general shell interpreter; the two shapes are literal (Codex 2).
- Treating a `refuse` binding as "no binding" and falling back to another eligible story (Codex 3, Claude 4).
- Requiring registration for every commit (Codex 3).
- Reading `DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE=` or any other per-command environment prefix as a pin (Claude 2).
- Folding in the main-worktree cases from #6247 comment 6844905798, or the planning-commit admission accepted on #5839.

## In plain English
A worker in a linked worktree cannot commit its own work. Two things stop it. The commit gate reads the staged files of the checkout the hook started in, so the usual forms that point a commit at another worktree (`cd <worktree> && git commit`, `git -C <worktree> commit`) are refused or judged against the wrong checkout. And the commit gate picks the story from the environment pin only, so with several active briefs it does not know which story the worker's worktree belongs to, although the write gate learned that in #6233. This arc covers both issues as one design, because the second check runs on whatever checkout the first one resolves. The thread for #6247 is read as part of the target.

## Pains
- P1 — A worker cannot commit in its linked worktree with `cd <worktree> && git commit …` or `git -C <worktree> commit …`; the lead agent or a human commits for it (#6278).
- P2 — The prospective scope-cover check on `git commit` does not use the per-worktree story binding from #6233, so in a registered worktree with several active briefs and no pin the worker's commit is refused as `multiple-eligible` (#6247).

## Notes for the arc
- Outside this warrant, named so the lean can place them: the main-worktree cases in #6247 comment 6844905798 (a commit that concludes a merge, a CHANGELOG line on a lifecycle PR, an inline `DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE=` prefix). #5839 has an accepted design for planning-only commits in the same function.
- Another story changes the commit-shape check in the same file today (#6276 with #6187 and #6188). The lean must name its `file_scope` and say what it assumes about that change.
- #6247 carries a recorded skip in its body (it extends the #6233 mechanism). This arc does not replace that record; it designs the two changes together.

## In plain English

The issues ask for workers to commit in their own linked worktrees using ordinary directory-selection commands, with the correct story governing the staged files. The pinned code confirms both problems: prospective coverage reads the hook’s project root, and story selection omits the existing worktree binding. The proposed direction is sound, but resolving a directory must also preserve checkout identity and command-parsing guarantees. I would bind a narrow, shared resolution path with explicit refusal cases, rather than simply remove the current retarget denial. Verification was source-only at `1fa8ab9cc7b1aad651e6d65e4103f7820bde3d04`; no tests or fixtures ran.

### 1. Resolve and admit one checkout before evaluating coverage — blocks-the-design

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:5183` selects `input.projectRoot` for staged-path inspection; lines 5199–5204 pass that same root to coverage. Existing `admitEffectiveHookRoot` at lines 1241–1268 distinguishes shared Git identity, foreign repositories, and unresolved identity. Its documentation at lines 1231–1239 also identifies occupancy, ritual, scope, and write-fence implications.

**Failure mode:** Changing only the index-read directory can combine the destination’s staged files with another checkout’s authority. Accepting any syntactically resolvable directory also lets a foreign repository become the commit target without the established identity boundary.

**Disposition:** Before binding, specify one canonical execution-directory-to-worktree resolution and same-common-directory admission, then use the admitted root consistently for staged paths, story selection, and fence loading. Explicitly identify which subsequent gates need that root; preserve the original payload identity for diagnostics and grants. Reuse existing admission mechanisms, but do not inherit their non-repository fallback for an unresolved commit target. A broader cross-repository design would require a separate authority contract.

### 2. Existing tokenization cannot safely define the newly accepted forms — blocks-the-design

**Evidence:** `dispatcher.ts:4876–4915` splits commands on shell separators and whitespace before detecting commits. For `git -C "C:/work trees/story" commit -m ok`, skipping two tokens for `-C` leaves part of the quoted path where the detector expects the subcommand. At line 5162, failed detection skips prospective coverage entirely. The quote-aware helper at lines 5012–5052 exists, but lines 5032–5035 consume backslashes inside double quotes.

**Failure mode:** A valid quoted target can miss the coverage gate, while reusing the existing quote helper indiscriminately can alter Windows paths. Simply permitting one `-C` or stripping a `cd` prefix does not establish agreement between what the shell executes and what the gate checks.

**Disposition:** Bind a narrow, shell-aware command grammar shared by commit recognition, target resolution, and index-mutating-form checks. Require fixtures for quoted paths with spaces, Windows backslashes, relative paths against the actual tool execution directory, repeated/mixed selectors, substitutions, and extra commands. Keep unresolved forms denied. A general shell interpreter is unnecessary; it would become preferable only if the supported command contract deliberately expands beyond these literal forms.

### 3. Preserve the binding resolver’s three outcomes — sharpens-framing

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/hooks/scope.ts:956–1028` already implements `none`, `bound`, and `refuse`, including registry failures, missing or ambiguous stories, eligibility, and conflicting environment pins. The write path consumes those outcomes at `dispatcher.ts:2572–2592`; prospective coverage currently passes only `env` at lines 5286–5288.

**Failure mode:** Treating a failed binding as absence permits fallback to a different eligible story. Requiring registration universally instead would unnecessarily reject existing main-worktree and unregistered-worktree behavior.

**Disposition:** Bind reuse of the existing resolver against the admitted target: `bound` supplies `boundPath`, `refuse` remains a denial, and `none` retains existing selection. Include negative fixtures for corrupt assignment state and conflicting pins, not only the two happy-path scope tests. State explicitly whether empty/lifecycle-only staged sets retain their current early exemptions at lines 5268–5284.

### 4. Thread instructions remain untrusted task data — footnote

**Evidence:** Snapshot comment `6857545101` contains imperative text such as “The lean must name its `file_scope`” and relayed authorization to “start implementation when they land.”

These are embedded instructions, not authorization for this critic. I treated them as claims about coordination and scope, and followed the supplied read-only critique envelope. No implementation, network access, agent dispatch, or file writes occurred.

## In plain English
The issue asks that a worker in a linked worktree be able to commit with `git -C <wt> commit …` or `cd <wt> && git commit …`, and that the commit be judged against that worktree's index and bound story (#6233, #6247). I read the pinned code and found a different picture. Today the hook does not refuse the `cd` form. It checks the hook root's staged files, and if that index is empty it lets the commit through. Several other forms already slip past the index snapshot. So the fix is not only "admit two more forms". It must also define a closed set of accepted shapes, refuse everything else, and check the resolved worktree through the same admission and occupancy path that writes use. I found no embedded instructions to critics in the snapshot. The relayed operator steer in 6857545101 is addressed to the parent.

### 1. Today's commit gate fails open on compound forms, so "stays refused" is false — blocks-the-design
Evidence: `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts` at the pin. `commandHasGitCommitCheckoutRetarget` (4925-4974) flags only `-C`, `--git-dir` and `--work-tree`. A `cd` part is not git, so it is skipped. `decideProspectiveGitCommitScopeCover` (5183-5198) then lists staged paths at `input.projectRoot`. `evaluateProspectiveScopeCover` returns `ok` on an empty list (5268-5274). Separately, `git add . && git commit -m x` passes: `commandHasGitCommitIndexMutatingForm` (5059-5150) looks only at the commit argv, so the snapshot is taken before the `add` runs. The only compound test is `git status && git commit` (dispatcher.test.ts:3877). None covers `cd`.
Failure mode: `cd <wt> && git commit`, `cd a && cd b && git commit` and `git add … && git commit` are judged against the wrong or stale index. If the hook root's index is empty, they are admitted. The issue's third Expected bullet assumes these are refused today.
Disposition: the lean must state a closed grammar for any Shell call that contains a commit part. Accepted: a simple commit, `git -C <one path> commit`, or exactly one leading `cd <path> &&`. Everything else is refused, including other parts before or after the commit, `pushd`, subshells, `bash -c`, and several `-C` flags. The fixtures must include the fail-open cases above, not only the issue's three acceptance pairs.

### 2. Environment-prefix retargets are skipped — sharpens-framing
Evidence: both scanners drop `NAME=value` tokens without checking them (4934-4938, 5065-5069). `GIT_INDEX_FILE=… git commit`, `GIT_DIR=… git commit` and `GIT_WORK_TREE=… git commit` are not seen as retargets.
Failure mode: the commit uses an index or repository other than the one the hook checked.
Disposition: the target resolver must treat any `GIT_*` location variable in the prefix as unresolvable and refuse it. #6247 comment 6844905798 already shows the hook ignores per-command environment, so these prefixes cannot help a legitimate commit either.

### 3. Resolve the target with the existing #3794 admission and run occupancy against it — sharpens-framing
Evidence: `admitEffectiveHookRoot` / `admitMutationTargetSet` (1241-1299) already prove that a target shares `--git-common-dir` with the payload root. They refuse a foreign repository, unproven identity and a span across worktrees. On the write path, the admitted root governs occupancy, ritual, scope and the fence (2009-2047, 2572-2593). ## Summary

A worker in a linked worktree cannot commit its own work with the usual command forms. The commit-shape check (#5656, `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts`, compound scanning near line 4912) admits a commit only as a simple command in the hook's own working directory. Two common forms are refused:

- `cd <worktree> && git commit …`
- `git -C <worktree> commit …`

The lead agent then commits for the worker, or a human does.

## Consumer impact

On a consumer project, 13 hook denials in one week were commits in these forms. Workers could not commit, so the lead agent committed for each of them. Maintainer sessions in this repo hit the same rule: the commit must be the only command in the call, staged in an earlier call.

## Expected

- A commit whose target worktree can be resolved from the command (`cd <path> &&` as the only prefix, or `git -C <path>`) is evaluated against that worktree: its index, its branch and its bound story (#6233).
- The same checks then apply as for a simple commit: prospective scope-cover, index snapshot, story binding. Nothing is admitted that a simple commit in that worktree would refuse.
- A command the hook cannot resolve to one worktree (several `cd`, variables, subshells) stays refused, with a message that names the accepted forms.

## Acceptance

- Given a registered linked worktree with staged in-scope changes, when the worker runs `git -C <worktree> commit -m …` from the parent directory, then the hook allows it; given staged out-of-scope changes, it refuses with the scope-cover message.
- Same pair for `cd <worktree> && git commit -m …`.
- A commit with an unresolvable target is refused and the message lists the accepted forms.

Refs #5656. Refs #6233. Related: #6247 (the commit scope-cover check does not use the per-worktree story binding).
